title: Unseen rescue-shift analytics dashboard
description: A previously unseen local data, document and visual-production mission; no task-specific application workflow is supplied.
objective: Turn the supplied rescue-shift CSV into independently reproducible analytics and a rendered visual dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: Persist metrics.json with exact totals, district comparisons, and the reproducible calculation method for the supplied CSV. CONTENT VERIFICATION (zlib inflate + PNG filter reconstruction of all scanlines): 499 distinct colours in a 4px sample grid, mean luma 28.18, 43424 bright pixels (4.712% of frame) confirming rendered text, 13262 green accent pixels confirming the styled cards/bar drew as designed => not a blank page and not a Chromium error page. Read the mission input CSV /home/nox/awe-group-cleanroom-20261112/reports/r1-generalization-1794714138208/state/artifacts/r1-generalization-98ebfb8a-0d70-4b58-a916-4384f2f7932f/input/rescue-shifts.csv (read-only), inspect its actual header and rows, and compute the exact aggregates. Persist metrics.json in the mission workspace root with exactly these top-level keys: row_count, scheduled_hours, completed_hours, incidents, completion_percent, districts. districts must be a JSON object keyed by district name, each value carrying that district's row count, scheduled_hours, completed_hours, incidents and completion_percent. Every count, hour total and percentage must be emitted as a JSON number (never a string, never quoted digits); completion_percent must be rounded/quantized to 2 decimal places as a number (e.g. 87.34). Include in the same metrics.json a 'method' field (string or object) that states the reproducible calculation recipe: the input path, the parsing rule, row_count = number of data rows, scheduled_hours = sum of the scheduled-hours column, completed_hours = sum of the completed-hours column, incidents = sum of the incidents column, completion_percent = completed_hours / scheduled_hours * 100 rounded to 2 dp, and the district grouping rule; add a 'columns' field mapping which CSV column fed each metric and a 'notes' field for any header normalisation or skipped/malformed rows, naming them explicitly. Cross-check the totals twice with two independent computations (one via python3 csv/json arithmetic, one via awk or sort/uniq aggregation) and confirm both agree to the last decimal before writing. Do not create any additional scripts or report files in the workspace; run the cross-check inline (python3 -c / awk one-liners) so the artifact set stays at metrics.json. Do not modify the CSV. No package installation, no network, no publishing.

Using the actual numbers read back from metrics.json (never re-derive or invent them), author a single self-contained dashboard.html in the mission workspace that visibly presents every metric: row_count, scheduled_hours, completed_hours, incidents, completion_percent, and a per-district comparison covering every district in the districts object with its row count, hour totals, incidents and completion percentage. Requirements: (a) zero external assets — no CDN, no <link> to remote CSS, no remote fonts, no external scripts, no remote images; all CSS inline in a <style> block and any iconography drawn with CSS/SVG/inline unicode data; use only locally-resolved font stacks (system-ui, sans-serif, monospace) so the 'load' event is immediate; (b) layout designed for a 1280x720 headless capture — a fixed-width ~1280px page with a compact header, a KPI card row for the five top-level metrics, and a district comparison table or bar visualisation that fits legibly in one viewport without clipping or scroll-dependent content, base font size >= 14px, sufficient contrast; (c) all percentages formatted to exactly 2 decimal places (e.g. 87.34%) and all hour totals formatted for readability while remaining faithful to the underlying numbers; (d) polished visual treatment — clear hierarchy, consistent spacing, restrained palette, visible labels and units. Then confirm self-containment mechanically: grep the file for 'http://', 'https://', 'src=', '@import' and report that no external reference remains, and validate the HTML parses (e.g. python3 -c with html.parser) so the render cannot land on a Chromium error page. criterion_checks.reason: metrics.json contains exactly the required top-level keys with numeric values: row_count 6, scheduled_hours 59, completed_hours 53, incidents 9, completion_percent 89.83, and districts as an object keyed North/South/West. I re-derived the arithmetic from the 6-row CSV: scheduled 12+8+10+14+6+9=59, completed 11+8+7+13+5+9=53, incidents 2+1+3+0+2+1=9, 53/59*100=89.8305->89.83; North 22/18/5->81.82, South 14/13/3->92.86, West 23/22/1->95.65 — all correct, all reconcile to global totals. No metric is a quoted string; the only string occurrences are descriptive text inside columns/method/notes documentation, which is appropriate. method block records input path, input sha256, parsing rule, per-formula derivations, district grouping rule, ROUND_HALF_UP rounding and a three-way cross-check (python csv, awk, coreutils) — a genuinely reproducible method. dashboard.html renders every percentage at two decimals (89.83%, 81.82%, 92.86%, 95.65%) and the legend range descriptor that previously read 0-100% was reworded during the design pass.
